newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa union warns of wider walkouts.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa union warns of wider walkouts.

text.p: A German union said Tuesday it was set to call a second and expanded wave of walkouts by employees over a wage dispute with the Deutsche Lufthansa AG airline.
The threat by the DAG white-collar union followed the breakdown Monday of the latest talks.
Ground and air staff represented by DAG last month held brief work stoppages that forced the cancellation of 35 flights and cost the airline 12 million German marks ($7.72 million).

"We shall make it clear that our anger has become greater," a DAG official told Reuters, adding that a greater number of airports would be affected and that the walk-outs would stretch to the maximum two hours allowed by law.
Sources close to airline staff said the protests were likely to hit international traffic next time as well as the domestic airports involved in the first protest.
They said that if Lufthansa refused to change its position as a result, a ballot on all-out strike action could follow.

DAG and the transport and public sector union OeTV, which represent the airline's 50,000 workers, said Lufthansa has still not offered its members a 1997 wage increase in line with others in the industry.

DAG is also angry that Lufthansa wants the new contracts to last 27 months instead of a year. Given the threat that many Lufthansa jobs could be moved abroad, the union would not tie itself to a two-year contract, DAG has said.
Lufthansa in a statement called for DAG to return to the negotiating table and call off the planned protests.
The DAG official said the new stoppages were certain to hit Frankfurt airport, the country's biggest, while Hamburg was also likely to be affected.
